title: Air India to Restore Most Suspended International Flights From September as Fleet Capacity Returns
excerpt: The Tata-owned carrier says Europe-bound operations will normalize from September, with Newark regaining frequencies, but Chicago and Washington routes remain grounded due to aircraft shortages.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Air India will restore most suspended international flights starting September, focusing on European routes.
  • Newark will see increased flight frequencies, while Chicago and Washington routes remain suspended.
  • Flight suspensions were due to aircraft shortages and delays in new deliveries.
  • New Airbus A350-1000 deliveries are expected by late 2026, enhancing long-haul capacity.
  • Air India continues to operate over 1,200 international flights monthly despite recent cuts.
  • Air India will restore most suspended international flights from September, with European operations expected to normalize first
  • Newark Liberty will regain additional frequencies as capacity returns, but Chicago O'Hare and Washington Dulles remain suspended
  • The suspensions stemmed from fleet retrofit delays, retirement of older Boeing 777-200LR aircraft, and delayed new deliveries
  • New Airbus A350-1000 deliveries are expected to begin toward the end of 2026, boosting long-haul capacity

Air India will progressively restore most of its suspended international flights beginning in September, the airline’s chief commercial officer Nipun Aggarwal confirmed, offering relief to diaspora travelers who have faced months of reduced service on key routes.

The Tata-owned carrier said European operations are expected to return to normal from September, while most frequency reductions across its global network will be progressively unwound through August. The majority of the September schedule is already on sale, allowing passengers to book in advance.

Flight Restoration Timeline
September 2023
Most suspended international flights restored, focusing on Europe.
August 2023
Progressive unwinding of frequency reductions across global network.
End of 2026
New Airbus A350-1000 deliveries expected to boost long-haul capacity.

What’s Coming Back — and What’s Not

Newark Liberty International Airport is among the destinations that will regain additional frequencies as more aircraft return to service. Flights from Delhi to Zurich, Tokyo, and Seoul are set for full restoration, with Zurich even gaining additional frequency.

However, two key U.S. destinations will remain offline for the foreseeable future. Chicago O’Hare and Washington Dulles services will stay suspended due to what Aggarwal described as aircraft shortages arising from the airline’s ongoing fleet retrofit program, the retirement of older Boeing 777-200LR aircraft, and delays in new aircraft deliveries.

“The aircraft that we were supposed to get have been delayed. The old aircraft were retired,” Aggarwal said, adding that deliveries of new aircraft, including the Airbus A350-1000, are expected to commence toward the end of the year.

Why Flights Were Cut

Air India announced the broad international pullback in May, reducing or temporarily suspending flights across North America, Europe, Australia, and Asia between June and August 2026. The airline cited continued airspace restrictions over certain regions — a reference to closures related to the Pakistan airspace situation — and record-high jet fuel prices that made several overseas routes financially unviable.

“The adjustments have been made in response to a combination of factors, including continued airspace restrictions over certain regions and record high jet fuel prices for international operations.”

— Air India official statement

At their peak, domestic capacity reductions hit 10-15%, though Aggarwal said those are already being wound down. Despite the cuts, Air India continued operating over 1,200 international flights per month, retaining 33 weekly flights to North America, 47 to Europe, 57 to the UK, and 158 across the Far East and Southeast Asia.

The Bigger Picture

The route restorations come against a backdrop of Air India’s ambitious transformation under Tata Group ownership. The airline group recorded estimated losses exceeding ₹22,000 crore in FY26, and Singapore Airlines has deepened its involvement as losses have mounted.

Aggarwal said the Pakistan airspace closure has no bearing on Air India’s aircraft acquisition plans, noting that orders have already been placed. The A350-1000 deliveries, expected late this year, will significantly boost the airline’s long-haul widebody capacity.

For NRI travelers, the September timeline offers a clearer planning window. Those flying to the U.S. East Coast can expect improved options through Newark, while passengers bound for Chicago or Washington will need to continue routing through alternative gateways or carriers until fleet availability improves.
